title: Drone Remote ID decoder, track table and TAK output
summary: Passive airspace awareness from broadcast Remote ID (ASTM F3411 / ASD-STAN EN 4709-002). A stdlib decoder for Open Drone ID messages and packs, validated field-for-field against opendroneid-core-c, extracts payloads from Wi-Fi beacon, Wi-Fi NAN and BLE captures, feeds a per-UAS track table with spoofing plausibility flags, and emits a UAS track plus operator point as Cursor-on-Target via PyTAK.
verified: Ran on 2026-11-06 (macOS arm64, Python 3.14.7 and 3.12.14, Apple clang 21). odid.py matched opendroneid-core-c master 849c03a field-for-field (exact float32/double values, raw string bytes) on 500 core-c-encoded messages/packs, 500 random raw messages, 81 unique payloads from the three public opendroneid/wireshark-dissector captures, plus a live 600-vector batch; 5 planted decoder mutations each failed the suite. capture.py decoded 42 NAN+beacon packs, 21 beacon packs with positions and 244 CRC-OK BT5 long-range packs from those captures. rid_to_cot.py sent 256 CoT events through PyTAK 7.6.1 to a local TCP sink (synthetic scenario) and 10 to a UDP sink (real beacon capture). Not verified: any live radio reception, a real TAK server or ATAK rendering, the core-c cmake build or its own odidtest (cmake absent; library compiled directly with cc), Auth message semantics beyond decoding, anomaly thresholds against real spoofing.
